content: I would have voted no. While raising the retirement age can help keep the pension system financially sustainable, a fixed age like 66 feels too blunt an instrument to measure readiness for retirement; tying it to actual changes in life expectancy would be fairer and adapt better to longer, healthier lives. A rigid cutoff risks penalizing those who stay active and healthy longer, and doesn’t truly reflect their ability to contribute and retire when it makes sense for them.
